solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Large-scale domicile very well off husband’s abandoned (7)

indicators.note: the husband is left behind, so his letter drops out

annotation.surface: An estate agent describing a vast mansion whose rich owner has walked out on the family.
annotation.walkthrough: Homeric means on the epic scale of Homer's poems; the clue reads like a property listing, so 'Large-scale' hides as an adjective for the house.
annotation.definitionFit: Homeric describes something grand and heroic in scale, like the battles of the Iliad.

entries.clue: Item of food in war vehicle that’s caught moving back (7)

indicators.note: the C shifts from the front of the word to a later spot

blocks.note: CHARIOT with its C lifted out
c = caught in cricket scoring; it goes back in after HARI

annotation.surface: A soldier finding a snack stuck inside a war chariot as it reverses.
annotation.walkthrough: The C of CHARIOT does not leave; it just moves back three places, turning the war vehicle into a bean.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: this is a single dried bean, the kind in baked beans, so one item of food.

entries.clue: Fellow taking care of wine (5)

indicators.note: the fellow takes the other letters inside himself

blocks.note: c/o, 'care of' on an envelope, gives CO

annotation.surface: A man put in charge of looking after the wine cellar.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Care of' reads as a phrase, but only 'care' feeds the letters (c/o) and 'of' links to the definition. Macon is a Burgundy wine town.
annotation.definitionFit: Macon (Mâcon) is a wine from the Mâconnais region of southern Burgundy.

entries.clue: Thus river rises, source of water for New Mexico location (7)

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means reading upwards, so backwards

annotation.surface: A description of a desert river springing up to water a town in New Mexico.
annotation.walkthrough: Roswell is the New Mexico town famous for the 1947 UFO incident. 'Source of water' looks like it wants a first letter, but it is a whole WELL.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: the town in south-east New Mexico known for the 1947 UFO story is a New Mexico location.

entries.clue: Diplomat and police investigator turned up to be asked for advice (9)

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up flips the letters to read upwards

annotation.surface: An envoy and a detective showing up to be asked for their opinions.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Turned up' sounds like arrived, which suits the surface; here it flips DET into TED.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to consult someone is to ask their advice, so the past participle matches 'asked for advice'.

entries.clue: Polish expert (4)

blocks.note: the verb: rub to a shine
a noun: an enthusiast who knows a subject inside out

annotation.surface: Someone from Poland with specialist knowledge.
annotation.walkthrough: The capital P, forced by starting the clue, makes 'Polish' look like the nationality; it is the verb.
annotation.definitionFit: Buff means both to polish and a knowledgeable enthusiast.

entries.clue: Depression when treated like disposable rubbish? (5)

blocks.note: rubbish is binned, so AS goes into BIN

annotation.surface: Someone feeling low because they have been thrown out like rubbish.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole phrase says 'binned': AS is treated like rubbish by being put in a BIN. 'Depression' is a hollow in the ground, not a mood.
annotation.definitionFit: A basin is a depression in land, like a river basin.

entries.clue: Mathematician putting together number that is right (7)

indicators.note: tells you to join the pieces end to end

annotation.surface: A mathematician assembling a number that turns out correct.
annotation.walkthrough: Joseph Fourier gave his name to Fourier series and transforms. 'Number' must be a specific word, FOUR.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Joseph Fourier, the Frenchman behind Fourier series, is one mathematician.

entries.clue: What acknowledges performance of USA involved in big business (8)

indicators.note: a performance of the letters puts them in a new order
the rearranged letters are wrapped up inside the company

annotation.surface: A review of how America performs as a big corporate player.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Performance' does double duty: it sits in the definition and also stirs up USA. Apple as 'big business' is typical Times shorthand.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: clapping is the audience's way of acknowledging a show when it ends.

entries.clue: Ragged father always attached to daughter (6)

indicators.note: the pieces are joined on to the daughter

blocks.note: aye is an old word for always

annotation.surface: A worn-out dad who is forever clinging to his daughter.
annotation.walkthrough: AYE here is the poetic 'ever', not 'yes'.
annotation.definitionFit: Frayed and ragged both describe worn, torn fabric.

entries.clue: About 100 American social workers who refuse to toe the line? (9)

definitions.text: who refuse to toe the line?
definitions.note: the definition is a relative clause standing for 'people who refuse to conform'

blocks.note: ants are social insects that work

annotation.surface: A report on a hundred American social workers who won't follow the rules.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Social workers' reads as a profession; it means insects living in colonies. Recusants were originally Catholics who refused to attend Church of England services.
annotation.definitionFit: Recusants are people who refuse to submit to authority or conform.

entries.clue: Meal — son’s taken drug (5)

indicators.note: the son is taken away, so his letter goes

blocks.note: S = son, taken away from the front

annotation.surface: A report that someone's son has taken drugs, set beside a meal.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Taken drug' reads as the son using drugs; 'taken' actually removes him, and 'drug' is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A slang sense: a stimulant such as amphetamine gets called this because it lifts you, the opposite of a downer.

entries.clue: Upset quiet canon yells as a result (15)

indicators.note: upsetting the letters knocks them into a new order

annotation.surface: A normally quiet clergyman is upset and starts shouting.
annotation.walkthrough: A canon is a cathedral clergyman; the surface has him losing his temper.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the adverb says something followed on from what came before, just as 'as a result' does.

entries.clue: You and I in fancy cloth, but not coat of church cloth (5)

indicators.note: fancy as a verb: the letters are reimagined in a new order
removes what follows from the word
WE goes inside the rearranged letters

blocks.clueFragment: fancy cloth, but not coat of church
blocks.note: CLOTH minus C and H (the outside of 'church') leaves LOT, rearranged to TOL
you and I together are we

annotation.surface: A couple wrapped in fancy fabric, but not in church vestments.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cloth' appears twice: the first is fodder, the second the definition. 'Coat of church' is its outer letters, C and H.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: the thing you dry yourself with after a bath is a piece of cloth.

entries.clue: Coverage of contemporary music performance on the radio (8)

indicators.note: broadcast, so heard rather than read

annotation.surface: Radio coverage of a modern music concert.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Coverage' feels like media reporting, which the radio surface backs up; it is the paper round a present.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: paper round a parcel is its covering, so coverage in the physical sense.

entries.clue: Sudden change that may be seen in modern Rutland (9)

definitions.text: Sudden change that may be seen in modern Rutland

blocks.note: reads like a shift in the weather or the landscape; it is a reversal of policy

blocks.clueFragment: that may be seen in modern Rutland
blocks.note: the county was abolished in 1974 and brought back in 1997, so today's Rutland exists only because a decision was undone

annotation.surface: A local historian spotting a dramatic shift in England's smallest county.
annotation.walkthrough: Rutland, England's smallest county, was abolished in 1974 and restored in 1997, so the county as it is now is the product of a turnround.
annotation.definitionFit: The clue reads straight: undoing the 1974 abolition and bringing the county back was a sudden reversal of policy.

entries.clue: Changing one’s mind, raving about church making comeback (9)

indicators.note: the raving goes round the church
the church letters come back, reading backwards

annotation.surface: A lapsed believer, ranting, is persuaded back to church.
annotation.walkthrough: Recanting is taking back a belief publicly; the surface's churchgoer returning fits nicely.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: withdrawing a belief you once held in public means you have changed your mind.

entries.clue: Sad choir arranged around piano displaying great enthusiasm (9)

indicators.note: the choir's letters are arranged like music, in a new order
the rearranged letters go round the piano

annotation.surface: A gloomy choir gathered round a piano, yet singing with gusto.
annotation.walkthrough: The musical surface is consistent: choir, arranged, piano. P sits inside the anagrammed letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: from rhapsody, an effusive outpouring, it describes speech or writing full of great enthusiasm.

entries.clue: Some Parisian in humdrum existence most likely to cause offence? (6)

indicators.note: the French word sits inside the rut

blocks.note: a rut is a dull routine

annotation.surface: A Parisian stuck in a boring routine becomes the most offensive person around.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Some Parisian' reads as a person from Paris; it means the word a Parisian uses for 'some'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym with a question mark: the most impolite remark is the one most likely to cause offence.

entries.clue: Not at home, mostly visiting island state in Borneo (7)

indicators.note: most of the word, with its last letter lost
a visitor is inside the island

blocks.note: Sark is one of the Channel Islands

annotation.surface: A traveller away from home, on a trip to an island state in Borneo.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Island' sounds like Borneo itself, but it is the tiny Channel Island of Sark.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: this Malaysian state occupies the north-west of the island of Borneo.

entries.clue: Town workers in group picked up (5)

indicators.note: picked up by the ear, as a signal is

blocks.note: a crew is a group of workers

annotation.surface: A town's workforce being collected in a group.
annotation.walkthrough: Crewe is a railway town in Cheshire, England. 'Picked up' reads as collected; it means heard.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: the Cheshire railway junction is a town, which is all the clue asks.

entries.clue: Longed, after joining firm, to be trained (7)

indicators.note: the first piece comes after the firm, joined on

blocks.note: to ache for is to long for

annotation.surface: A new recruit, keen to be trained after joining a company.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Joining firm' reads as starting a job; here it just places CO first.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a coach trains athletes or pupils, so to have been coached is to have been trained.

entries.clue: Tear you’d inserted in opening up? (3-4)

indicators.note: puts one piece inside another
in a down clue, reading upward means backwards

blocks.note: a pore is an opening in the skin
ye'd, the old form of you'd

annotation.surface: A rip in a garment, with you pushing into a gap as it is lifted.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tear' rhymes with 'wear' in the surface; it is the one that rhymes with 'ear'.
annotation.definitionFit: A literal description: a teardrop is one drop of liquid from the eye, so the hyphenated phrase spells out what a tear is.

entries.clue: Intemperate lads sorted out, put into separate groups (15)

indicators.note: the letters are sorted into a new order

annotation.surface: Drunken young men being split up by a bouncer.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sorted out' in the surface means dealt with firmly; for the solver it rearranges the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: splitting an organisation into departments puts its people into separate groups.

entries.clue: French artist intended putting down English (5)

indicators.note: in a down clue, the E is put lower down the word

blocks.note: MEANT with its E lifted out
E = English, placed one step further down

annotation.surface: A French painter who meant to disparage the English.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Putting down' reads as insulting; in this down clue it moves the E lower, so MEANT becomes MANET.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Édouard, painter of Olympia and a forerunner of Impressionism, is one French artist.

entries.clue: Press guy’s ending mocking language (5)

indicators.note: take only the last letter of guy

annotation.surface: A newspaper man's closing remarks full of mockery.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Press guy' suggests a journalist; the press is a verb, the laundry kind.
annotation.definitionFit: Irony is language that says the opposite of what it means, often to mock.

entries.clue: Four distinct points comprising current source of strength (5)

indicators.note: the four letters hold the current between them

blocks.note: the compass points S, N, E, W
I is the symbol for electric current

annotation.surface: An engineer describing four contact points that carry a current to power something.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Distinct' tells you the four points are separate letters, free to be placed in any order.
annotation.definitionFit: Sinews are tendons, and figuratively the source of strength.

entries.clue: Beastly noise and bad smell — old city person who lives close by? (9)

annotation.surface: A complaint about a noisy, smelly person living next door.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a neighbour dispute, so the definition sits in plain sight; 'beastly' means from an animal, not nasty.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: the person next door or down the street lives close by; the question mark flags the loose phrasing.

entries.clue: Pose with king in satirical sketch (4)

indicators.note: the pose takes the king in with it

blocks.note: to sit or pose for a portrait

annotation.surface: Striking a pose alongside a king in a comedy sketch.
annotation.walkthrough: Pose here is sitting for an artist.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a short comic piece sending something up is a satirical sketch.

entries.clue: Feeling unstable on horse? Go faster! (5-2)

blocks.note: a rider on horseback is up

annotation.surface: A nervous rider, wobbly in the saddle, being urged to speed up.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole surface is a riding lesson, and the answer is what a rider shouts to spur the horse on.
annotation.definitionFit: Giddy-up is the call urging a horse to go faster.
